## PHASE: reviewer
## ISSUE: 236

### Issue Details
## Issue #236

## Parent

#231 ([PRD] Staff Member CRUD with Analytics Dashboard)

## What to build

Create the staff member detail page at `/staff/:id` showing a profile card, four core statistics in a metrics row, and a repair history table. Clicking any staff member from the list navigates here. The stats are fetched in parallel with the profile via `Promise.all`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Frontend route `/staff/:id` registered and linked from list page (click on name or row navigates to detail)
- [ ] Profile card displays: name, role badge, hourly rate (€X.XX/h), active/inactive status with toggle switch, createdAt date
- [ ] Stats row displays four metrics in a horizontal grid: total hours worked (formatted as Xh Ym), repairs completed (count), active repairs (count), avg repair duration (formatted or "N/A" if zero completions)
- [ ] Stats fetched via `GET /users/:id/stats` endpoint; loading state shown while fetching (skeleton or spinner)
- [ ] Repair history table below stats showing: repair ID/number, bicycle info (brand/model), status badge, assigned date, completion date. Data sourced from existing repairs API (`GET /repairs?assignedTo=...`)
- [ ] Repair history supports basic filtering by status dropdown (all/completed/in-progress/cancelled)
- [ ] "Back to list" navigation link at top of page
- [ ] 404 handling: if staff member not found, show error state with back button

## Out of scope

- **Edit forms on detail page** — No inline editing of name, role, or hourly rate. CRUD via modal dialog is deferred to a later slice (per PRD #231).
- **Toggle switch functionality** — The active/inactive toggle is display-only (read-only visual indicator). Functional toggle via PATCH endpoint is deferred to the CRUD modal slice.
- **Repair history pagination** — Show all repairs for the staff member without pagination controls. If count exceeds ~50, simple truncation or "showing first N" note is acceptable.
- **Export features** — No CSV/PDF export of repair history or stats.
- **Revenue attribution** — Not included per PRD #231 out-of-scope list.

## Test expectations

Follow existing patterns from `client/src/features/repairs/components/__tests__/`:

- **No component tests required** for this slice (consistent with PRD #231 testing decisions: "Frontend component tests — no existing component test pattern in codebase; deferred.")
- If builder chooses to add tests, follow the hook-testing pattern from `client/src/features/customers/hooks/__tests__/useCustomers.test.ts`

## Implementation references

### Detail page patterns (prior art)
- **RepairDetailPage**: `client/src/features/repairs/components/RepairDetailPage.tsx` — Full detail page with profile header, stats sections, and data tables. Uses `useParams()` + `useNavigate()`. Shows loading spinner and error state with back button.
- **QuoteDetailView**: `client/src/features/quotes/components/QuoteDetailView.tsx` — Simpler wrapper pattern: extracts `id` from params, delegates to a panel component.

### Navigation patterns (list → detail)
- **RepairListPage row click**: `client/src/features/repairs/components/RepairListPage.tsx` (~line 290) — `<tr onClick={() => navigate(\`/repairs/${repair.id}\`)}>` pattern for clickable rows.

### Router registration
- **App router**: `client/src/app/App.tsx` — Add `{ path: '/staff/:id', element: <StaffDetailPage /> }` to children array alongside existing routes.

### Backend endpoints (to be provided by blocked issues)
- **GET /users/:id/stats** — Provided by #235. Returns `{ totalHoursWorked, completedRepairs, activeRepairs, avgRepairDurationMinutes }`.
- **GET /repairs?assignedTo=...** — Existing endpoint in `server/src/routes/repairs.ts` (~line 40). Supports `status` filter and pagination via `page`/`pageSize`.

### Repair status enum (for filter dropdown)
- **Source**: `client/src/features/repairs/types.ts` → `RepairStatus = 'intake' | 'in_progress' | 'on_hold' | 'verified' | 'ready' | 'completed' | 'cancelled'`
- **Filter mapping**: AC says "all/completed/in-progress/cancelled" — map to: `''` (all), `'completed'`, `'in_progress'`, `'cancelled'`

### UI components available
- **Card/CardHeader/CardContent**: `client/src/components/ui/card.tsx` — For profile card layout
- **Switch**: `client/src/components/ui/switch.tsx` — Radix Switch for display-only toggle (use `disabled={true}`)
- **DataTable**: `client/src/components/ui/DataTable.tsx` — Reusable paginated table component

### Users schema reference
- **Schema**: `server/src/db/schema.ts` (~line 69) — `users` table: `id`, `name`, `role` (enum: mechanic|manager), `hourlyRate` (integer cents), `isActive` (boolean), `createdAt` (timestamp)

### Duration formatting
- **Prior art**: `RepairDetailPage.tsx` → `formatDuration(ms)` helper converts milliseconds to "Xh Ym" format. Reuse this pattern for total hours worked display.

## Blocked by

- #232 (Staff Member List Page — needs the foundation types and API client pattern)
- #235 (Staff Stats Computation — needs the GET /users/:id/stats endpoint to be available)

## Parent PRD (#231)

## Problem Statement

The shop has no way to manage its staff members (mechanics and managers) through the application. The `users` table exists in the database and is referenced by repairs (`assignedTo`) and work logs (`userId`), but there is only a single read-only endpoint returning active workers for dropdown selectors. There is no create, edit, or soft-delete capability, and no visibility into individual staff performance (hours worked, repairs completed).

## Solution

A full CRUD feature for Staff Members with a dedicated frontend page at `/staff`. The list view shows all staff in a paginated DataTable with search. Clicking a staff member opens a detail page showing their profile, four core statistics (total hours worked, repairs completed, active repairs, average repair duration), and a repair history table. Create and edit are handled via a Radix Dialog modal. Deletion is soft-only (`isActive = false`), preserving historical data integrity for repairs and work logs.

## User Stories

1. As a manager, I want to see a list of all staff members (active and inactive), so that I can manage the team roster
2. As a manager, I want to search the staff list by name, so that I can quickly find a specific person
3. As a manager, I want to create a new staff member with name, role, and hourly rate, so that they appear in assignment dropdowns
4. As a manager, I want to edit an existing staff member's details (name, role, hourly rate), so that their information stays current
5. As a manager, I want to toggle a staff member's active/inactive status, so that inactive workers disappear from assignment dropdowns without losing historical data
6. As a manager, I want to view a detail page for each staff member, so that I can see their full profile and performance at a glance
7. As a manager, I want to see total hours worked per staff member (from work log timers), so that I can track time investment
8. As a manager, I want to see the number of repairs completed by each staff member, so that I can gauge workload distribution
9. As a manager, I want to see how many active (in-progress) repairs each staff member has assigned, so that I can balance workloads
10. As a manager, I want to see average repair duration per staff member, so that I can identify efficiency patterns
11. As a manager, I want to see a table of repairs handled by a specific staff member on their detail page, so that I can review their work history
12. As a mechanic, I want my name and role displayed correctly in the system, so that repair assignments are accurate
13. As an operator, I want soft-delete (not hard-delete) for staff members, so that historical repairs and work logs remain attributable to real people

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain Terminology
- **"Staff Member"** is the canonical domain term. The database table remains `users`. The API path remains `/api/users` (no rename). UI labels use "Staff Members".

### Backend Modules
- **Expanded `users.service.ts`** — Add `createUser`, `getUserById`, `updateUser`, `listUsersPaginated`, and soft-delete via PATCH setting `isActive = false`. Existing `getActiveWorkers()` is preserved for dropdown consumers.
- **New staff stats computation module** — Deep, pure function: `computeStaffStats(userId)` aggregates from `workLogs` (timer sessions) and `repairs` to produce `{ totalHoursWorked: number, completedRepairs: number, activeRepairs: number, avgRepairDurationMinutes: number | null }`. No side effects.
- **No hard delete endpoint** — PATCH `/users/:id` with `{ isActive: false }` serves as soft delete. No DELETE route is added.

### API Endpoints (on `/api/users`)
| Method | Route | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| GET | `/users?search=&page=&pageSize=` | Paginated list; falls back to compact dropdown shape when no params present |
| GET | `/users/:id` | Single staff member detail |
| POST | `/users` | Create new staff member |
| PATCH | `/users/:id` | Update (name, role, hourlyRate, isActive) |
| GET | `/users/:id/stats` | Staff stats aggregation (dedicated endpoint, fetched in parallel with profile on detail page) |

### Shared Layer
- **`shared/types/staff.ts`** — `StaffMember`, `NewStaffMember`, `UpdateStaffMember`, `StaffStats` interfaces. Golden copy used by both frontend and backend.
- **`shared/validations/staff.ts`** — Zod schemas for create and update inputs. Role is enum (`mechanic` | `manager`). Hourly rate validated as positive integer (cents/hour).

### Frontend Feature: `client/src/features/staff/`
- `api.ts` — API client functions for all CRUD + stats endpoints
- `hooks/useStaffMembers.ts` — Data fetching hook using TanStack Query or fetcher pattern consistent with existing features
- `components/StaffListPage.tsx` — Paginated DataTable (25/page) with inline search, columns: name, role, hourly rate, active status toggle
- `components/StaffDetailPage.tsx` — Profile card + stats row (4 metrics) + repair history table. Route: `/staff/:id`
- `components/StaffFormDialog.tsx` — Radix Dialog modal for create/edit mode. Fields: name, role selector, hourly rate input

### Schema Changes
- **No schema changes required.** The `users` table already has all needed columns: `id`, `name`, `role`, `hourlyRate`, `isActive`, `createdAt`.

### Authorization
- No auth guards. Consistent with app-wide deferred authorization policy documented in CONTEXT.md.

## Testing Decisions

### What Makes a Good Test
Test external behavior and outcomes, not implementation details. Verify that given specific input data, the correct output is produced. Do not test internal query construction or private helper functions.

### Modules to Test
- **Staff stats computation** — Deep module with pure logic. Test: zero repairs (returns nulls/zeros), single repair with one work log, multiple repairs with overlapping timers, cancelled repairs excluded from completed count. Prior art: `repair-timer.test.ts` in `server/src/services/__tests__/`.
- **Service CRUD functions** — Test create validates role enum and positive hourly rate; update toggles isActive correctly; paginated list respects search filter and page boundaries. Prior art: `customer-crud.test.ts` in `server/src/services/__tests__/`.

### Out of Scope for Testing
- Frontend component tests — no existing component test pattern in codebase; deferred.
- Integration/E2E tests — deferred until core unit tests pass.

## Out of Scope

- Authentication / login system (deferred globally)
- Role-based access control on routes or UI (deferred globally)
- Revenue attribution per staff member (would require joining through `repairLineItems`; can be added later)
- Parts usage tracking per worker
- Payroll integration or export
- Bulk operations (import/export CSV for staff roster)
- Calendar/timeline view of staff availability

## Further Notes

- The existing `GET /users` compact response (used by repair assignment dropdowns) must continue to work unchanged. Paginated mode is activated only when query parameters are present, matching the Customer route pattern.
- Hourly rate is stored in cents/hour (integer), consistent with all pricing fields in the schema. Frontend should display as currency (e.g., "€45.00/h").
- Stats computation queries `workLogs` for timer sessions where `userId = staffMemberId` and `endedAt IS NOT NULL`. Running timers (null `endedAt`) are excluded from totals.

## BUILDER COMPLETED

---
name: reviewer
description: Reviews code, structure, and decisions for consistency, maintainability, and correctness. Use when pre-merge review, scope verification, boundary checks, naming consistency, rule compliance validation
---

# Reviewer

## Quick start

Evaluate whether the result is correct, safe, consistent, and maintainable. The reviewer protects project quality — working code is not necessarily good code.

**Input:** implemented slice, planner brief, architect guidance, conventions, ADRs, acceptance criteria  
**Output:** review findings with approval status

---

## Workflows

### Default Review Process

1. Review the task goal and acceptance criteria
2. Compare implementation against scope — flag scope creep
3. Check structure and domain boundaries
4. Check naming consistency and readability
5. Check for duplication and unnecessary complexity
6. Verify alignment with project rules and conventions
7. Determine if documentation or ADR updates are needed
8. Approve, reject, or request fixes

### Pre-Review Checklist

Before finishing, verify:

- [ ] Result matches requested scope
- [ ] Project rules respected
- [ ] Domain boundaries intact
- [ ] Naming consistent with codebase
- [ ] Code is understandable without extra context
- [ ] No unnecessary duplication
- [ ] Hidden assumptions made visible
- [ ] Solution is maintainable, not clever
- [ ] Docs or ADR updates identified

**Definition of Done:** Quality and safety are clearly understood; next action is obvious.

---

## Guardrails

### Allowed Actions

- Review code and plans
- Flag rule violations
- Identify duplication
- Suggest refactors
- Detect boundary problems
- Request clarification of assumptions
- Check whether docs should be updated
- Approve or reject a result

### Forbidden Actions

- Rewriting everything without reason
- Redesigning the whole system during normal review
- Expanding scope
- Approving risky work only because it functions
- Ignoring domain or structural issues

### Shell Safety Rules

#### grep / xargs — Suppress False-Positive Errors

When checking for **absence** of patterns (e.g. "are there still inline `/ 100`?"), `grep` returns exit code 1 on no matches and `xargs` can return 123. Both are flagged as errors by the session parser even though they mean success.

**Always append `|| true` to grep/xargs used for absence checks:**

```bash
# ❌ Bad — exit code 1 flagged as error when no matches found
grep -rn '/ 100' server/src/api/

# ✅ Good — always exits 0, output still shows any matches
grep -rn '/ 100' server/src/api/ || true

# ✅ Good — xargs with grep, suppress exit code 123
find . -name "*.ts" | xargs grep -l 'pattern' 2>/dev/null || true
```

**Preferred tool:** Use `.pi/skills/reviewer/scripts/grep-safe.sh` instead of raw `grep` for absence checks. It always exits 0 and annotates results:

```bash
# ✅ Best — uses grep-safe, always exits 0, prints "✓ no matches found" when clean
bash .pi/skills/reviewer/scripts/grep-safe.sh -rn '/ 100' server/src/api/
```

**Fallback:** If you can't reach the script, use `|| true`.

**Rule:** If the desired outcome is "no output = good", **never let raw grep exit code propagate**.

#### Project Structure — Verify Before Searching

This project does NOT have a flat `src/` directory. Top-level source directories are:

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|
| `server/src/` | Backend API, services, DB layer |
| `client/src/` | Frontend (React) |
| `shared/` | Shared types, validations, utilities |
| `drizzle/` | Database migrations |

**Before running `find` or `grep`:**
1. Know which directory your target lives in — don't guess `/src`
2. If unsure, run `ls /home/david/projects/pi-pos-v0/` first (one command, saves retries)
3. Tests live alongside source: `server/__tests__/`, not root `__tests__/`

### Bash Timeout Rule

When running tests or type checks via bash, **always set explicit short timeouts**:

| Command | Max timeout |
|---------|-------------|
| `pnpm test` (full workspace) | 10s — too slow for review |
| `pnpm test server` (server only) | 15s |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 15s |
| Single test file (`vitest run <file>`) | 15s |

**Why:** The hard timeout gate kills commands at 60–120s, which strips all output. A short timeout gives you clean failure output to reason about.

**If a command times out:** Note it in the review and proceed with manual code inspection. Do not retry with longer timeouts — the Reviewer's job is assessment, not test debugging.

### Review Rules

- Working ≠ good — prefer maintainability over cleverness
- Protect project consistency above all
- Flag hidden assumptions explicitly
- Keep feedback concrete, not abstract
- Separate critical issues from optional improvements

---

## Output Format

Every review should contain:

1. **Summary** — one-line assessment of the result
2. **Critical Issues** — must fix before merge
3. **Medium Issues** — should fix, blocks polish
4. **Minor Improvements** — nice to have
5. **Rule Violations** — specific convention breaches
6. **Documentation Impact** — what needs updating
7. **Approval Status** — one of the four states below

### Approval States

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `approved` | Ready to merge |
| `approved with minor fixes` | Merge after cosmetic/non-blocking changes |
| `changes required` | Must address critical/medium issues before re-review |
| `rejected due to structural conflict` | Requires architect or DB engineer input |

### Example Review Output

```
## Review: Product API (`server/src/api/products.ts`)

**Summary:** CRUD endpoints are functional and follow project conventions, but have
inconsistent price conversion handling between create/update routes.

### Critical Issues
- None

### Medium Issues
- `PUT /:id` converts cents→dollars in response but `POST /` returns raw cents — 
  response shape is inconsistent across methods
- No validation that `quantityOnHand` is non-negative on update

### Minor Improvements
- Extract price conversion to shared util (`Math.round(x * 100)` repeated 3x)
- Add JSDoc for query param types in GET handler

### Rule Violations
- None

### Documentation Impact
- API docs should clarify that POST returns cents, PUT returns dollars

**Approval:** `approved with minor fixes`
```

---

## Handoff

| To | When |
|----|------|
| `typescript-implementer` | Fixes needed on code level |
| `architect` | Structural conflict or boundary violation found |
| `db-engineer` | Schema mismatch, data integrity concern, or migration issue |
| documentation flow | ADRs, API docs, or conventions need updating |

## Review: Staff Detail Page (#236)

**Summary:** Frontend implementation is well-structured and follows project conventions, but depends on a missing backend route (`GET /users/:id`) that prevents the detail page from loading profile data.

### Critical Issues

1. **Missing `GET /users/:id` server route** — The frontend calls `fetchStaffMemberById(id)` → `/api/users/${id}`, but no such GET endpoint exists in `server/src/routes/users.ts`. Only `GET /`, `POST /`, `PATCH /:id`, and `GET /:id/stats` are defined. The detail page will 404 on profile fetch until this route is added.

### Medium Issues

- None

### Minor Improvements

1. **Duplicate type definition** — `RepairHistoryRow` in `StaffDetailPage.tsx` (line 27) mirrors `StaffRepair` from `api.ts` (line 95). Import and reuse `StaffRepair` instead of redefining it locally.
2. **Double cast on repair data** — Line 147: `response.repairs as unknown as RepairHistoryRow[]`. Using the shared `StaffRepair` type would eliminate this double cast entirely.

### Rule Violations

- None

### Acceptance Criteria Verification

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Route `/staff/:id` registered + linked from list | ✅ Routes in App.tsx, clickable name navigates |
| 2 | Profile card: name, role badge, hourly rate (€X.XX/h), active/inactive toggle, createdAt | ✅ All present, toggle is `disabled={true}` |
| 3 | Stats row: total hours (Xh Ym), repairs completed, active repairs, avg duration (N/A if zero) | ✅ Four StatCards with correct formatting |
| 4 | Stats via `GET /users/:id/stats`; loading skeleton shown | ✅ Promise.all + skeleton loaders |
| 5 | Repair history table: ID, bicycle info, status badge, assigned/completion dates | ✅ Table present with all columns |
| 6 | Status filter dropdown (all/completed/in-progress/cancelled) | ✅ Select element with correct mapping |
| 7 | "Back to list" navigation link | ✅ ArrowLeft button navigating to `/staff` |
| 8 | 404 handling: error state + back button | ✅ Error/404 render block present |

### Code Quality Notes

- **No `any` types** in production code ✅
- **Domain terminology** consistent with CONTEXT.md ("Staff Member") ✅
- **Toggle switch is read-only** (`disabled={true}`) per out-of-scope decision ✅
- **Error handling**: stats failure is non-fatal (partial page shown), profile failure shows error state ✅
- **TypeScript compiles clean** for staff feature (pre-existing errors in quotes only) ✅

### Documentation Impact

- Backend `users.ts` routes need a `GET /:id` handler added before this slice is functional end-to-end.
